Own-side guiding as a different stiffness path
For an introduced single-column small-angle model, a soft rotational end spring contributes .5*ktheta*theta^2 and compression contributes -.5*P*l*theta^2. At P8450N,l=.27m,ktheta1000Nm/rad, the tangent is -1281.5Nm/rad. Without a guide the represented unbraced length must be less than.118343m for positivity.

A lateral guide at lever a adds .5*kguide*a^2*theta^2. At a=.1m its neutral threshold is128150N/m; strict positivity requires more. Threshold guide force at1mrad is12.815N. At .05m the threshold is512600N/m; at .15m56955.6N/m.
This is a candidate own-side support principle, not a supplied bearing or guide. Its frame, off-axis reactions, geometry, contact/backlash, installed stiffness and loss-of-power state must be constructed. It cannot cross an allegedly isolated cut, or hide a moment path around a force sensor. The calculation does not prove full-column buckling strength or replacement-joint stability.
